finding_resolutions.explanation: Added an owner-controlled reset entry point acceptance criterion and matching restart validation requirement to encounter-admission-cap-enforcement, closing the sole gap among run-persistent owners.

Added an acceptance criterion to five-room-content-authoring requiring authored sealed-door connectivity between the five spaces and designation of the Final Room's exit as the final door. Placed on five-room-content-authoring rather than dungeon-encounter-content-authoring because room connectivity is a room-geometry property ('each room ends at a door') and encounter authoring's own language ('per-door durability values') presupposes door instances already exist; this is a graph-representation decision within refiner authority, not a genuinely unresolved design question.

Added Bone Archive lane-navigability and Chapel of Ash occlusion-geometry validation requirements to five-room-content-authoring so both the authoring side and the runtime/navigation side own their half of each joint check.

Added an acceptance criterion to dungeon-encounter-content-authoring making Ranged Enemy's first-introduction-in-Chapel-of-Ash pacing (and melee-only Ruined Entry/Bone Archive) an obliging requirement rather than only gdd_evidence prose.

Added a new typed pipeline_constraint non_code_requirement, 'Schedule-slip scope-reduction order', capturing the GDD's bounded Weeks 5-6 fallback: stretch features cut first, then advanced door visuals/one encounter variation, then final-room density toward the low end of 3-8 with simplified presentation polish, with required systems never cut.

Restated the room-space consumption prerequisite inside dungeon-encounter-content-authoring's decomposition_reason field (in addition to the existing notes text) so a future Progressive Decomposer is durably instructed to attach the real edge once concrete descendants exist, without introducing an illegal feature-to-feature dependency now.

Removed the three-to-eight-enemies validation requirement from encounter-admission-cap-enforcement (which cannot exercise authored-content sizing from its own scope) and added the matching validation requirement to dungeon-encounter-content-authoring, which owns and can exercise that property.

Resolved by the same acceptance criterion added under CE-04 on dungeon-encounter-content-authoring requiring Ranged Enemy's first introduction in Chapel of Ash alongside Melee support, with Ruined Entry/Bone Archive remaining melee-only.

Resolved by the same acceptance criterion added under CE-02 on five-room-content-authoring requiring forward-only sealed-door connectivity between the five spaces and designation of the Final Room's exit as the final door.
Resolved by the same new 'Schedule-slip scope-reduction order' pipeline_constraint added under CE-05, giving the Weeks 5-6 scope-cut fallback a durable typed representation.

result.reasoning: Reviewed the ten CE findings against the frozen candidate (encounter-admission-cap-enforcement, five-room-content-authoring, dungeon-encounter-content-authoring, floor-run-restart-persistent-closure, doors, final-escape-victory) and the GDD (Section 3 Dungeon Floor Structure, Section 5 Six-Week Development Plan, Floor-run restart ownership, Active Enemy Registry and Encounter Admission, Player Experience Success Criteria). All 10 findings were credible representation gaps confirmed by direct comparison against candidate line content and real GDD text (verified the Six-Week Development Plan scope-cut sentence and Dungeon Floor Structure room descriptions directly in Docs/GDD/No_Safe_Circle_GDD.md). Applied minimal field-level corrections: (1) gave encounter-admission-cap-enforcement the missing owner-side reset criterion/validation matching every other persistent owner; (2) gave five-room-content-authoring the missing door-connectivity acceptance criterion, choosing that feature over dungeon-encounter-content-authoring because room connectivity is geometry-level and encounter authoring's own text presupposes doors already exist; (3) split the Bone Archive/Chapel of Ash joint validation checks so the authoring side is obliged, not just the runtime/navigation/attack side; (4) added the Ranged-Enemy-introduced-in-Chapel-of-Ash pacing criterion; (5) added a new typed pipeline_constraint for the Six-Week Plan's bounded scope-reduction fallback; (6) moved the room-space consumption note into the durable decomposition_reason field without creating an illegal feature-target dependency; (7) relocated the 3-8 enemy sizing validation from the admission item (which cannot exercise it) to the authoring item that owns it. The two deterministic CE-R16/CE-R21/CE-R22 findings duplicate CE-04/CE-02/CE-05 respectively and were resolved by the same corrections. No finding required rejection or an unresolved question — none conflicted with canon, and CE-02's human-review flag concerned only which of two deferred features should host the criterion, a graph-representation choice within refiner authority given the room-geometry ownership already established by the candidate's own text.
